title: All Changes May Have Invariant Principles: Improving Ever-Shifting Harmful Meme Detection via Design Concept Reproduction

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models' (MLLMs) detection accuracy and F1-score on the 'Racism' subset of the GOAT-Bench meme dataset and temporal-evolving Twitter datasets, utilizing a Design Concept Graph (DCG) to explain underlying racist stereotypes.

Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models' (MLLMs) detection accuracy and F1-score on the 'Misogyny' subset of meme datasets, identifying implicit misogynistic slangs, objectification, and gender stereotypes using reproduced design concepts.
Categorizing and detecting national stereotypes, xenophobia, and national conflicts in multimodal memes using the predefined typology hierarchy of the Design Concept Graph (DCG).
Categorizing and detecting religious stereotyping, inter-religious conflict, and blasphemy (e.g., sacred symbol misuse) in memes using the predefined 'Religion' macro-type typology.
Classifying disability mockery and stereotypes under the 'Human' macro-type in the fail reason tree and Design Concept Graph (DCG) to improve model recognition of marginalized group discrimination.
Identifying cultural appropriation, ethnic stereotyping, and heritage disrespect in memes using the 'Culture' macro-type of the Design Concept Graph (DCG) to guide model detection.
Detecting propaganda, political hate speech, conspiracy theories, and leader mockery using the 'Political' macro-type classification to analyze the underlying design concepts of political memes.
